In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Surah Hud

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm, then elaborated, from the presence of One who is All-Wise, All-Aware.﴾

Know that the scholars have differed greatly regarding the meaning of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) at the beginnings of the surahs, and the inductive study (istiqra') of the Great Qur'an favors one of those opinions. We will mention the disagreement and what the Qur'an favors among them by induction, so we say, and in Allah, Mighty and Exalted, we seek help:

Some scholars said: they are among the things whose knowledge Allah, Exalted, has reserved for Himself, as we have explained in "Al 'Imran." Among those reported to have held this view are Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them all, as well as 'Amir al-Sha'bi, Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, and Abu Hatim ibn Hibban, who chose this view.

It was also said: they are names of the surahs with which they begin. Among those who said this is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and what indicates this view is narrated from Mujahid, Qatadah, and Zayd ibn Aslam. al-Zamakhshari said in his tafsir: "And the majority are agreed upon it." It is also reported from Sibawayh that he explicitly stated it. This view is strengthened by what is established in the Sahih from Abu Hurayrah: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the Fajr prayer on Friday Alif-Lam-Mim As-Sajdah [al-Sajdah: 1] and Hal ata 'ala al-insan [al-Insan: 1]."

It is also indicated by the words of the slayer of Muhammad al-Sajjad ibn Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, on the day of the Camel. He was Shurayh ibn Abi Awfa al-'Absi, as mentioned by al-Bukhari in his Sahih at the beginning of Surah al-Mu'min:

*It reminds me of Ha-Mim while the spear is interlaced, so why did he not recite Ha-Mim before the advance?*

Ibn Ishaq related that this verse belongs to al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i, saying that he is the one who killed Muhammad ibn Talhah mentioned. Abu Mikhnaf mentioned that it belongs to Mudlij ibn Ka'b al-Sa'di, and it is said Ka'b ibn Mudlij. al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar mentioned that most agree that the one who killed him was 'Isam ibn Muq'shi'irr. al-Marzubani said: "And this is the firm (report)," and he recited the verse mentioned, and before it:

*And a man with unkempt hair, constant in the verses of his Lord, little harmful, as far as the eye can see, a Muslim.*

*I tore open with the spear the collar of his shirt, so he fell prostrate, onto his hands and his mouth,*

*for nothing, except that he did not follow 'Ali; and whoever does not follow the truth will regret.*

"It reminds me of Ha-Mim..." the verse. End of quotation from Fath al-Bari.

So his saying "yudhakkiruni Ha-Mim" (it reminds me of Ha-Mim), with "Ha-Mim" declined as an indeclinable noun, indicates what we have mentioned, that it is a name of the surah.

It was also said: they are among the names of Allah, Exalted. Among those who said this are Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, al-Sha'bi, and Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi the Elder. Its meaning is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. And from him too: that they are oaths which Allah swore by, and they are among His names. Something similar is reported from 'Ikrimah.

It was also said: they are letters, each one of which is from one of the names of Allah, Mighty and Exalted. So the Alif in "Alif-Lam-Mim," for example, is the key to the Name Allah; the Lam is the key to His Name Latif; the Mim is the key to His Name Majid; and so on. This is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, and Abu al-'Aliyah. This view is supported by the argument that the Arabs sometimes use a single letter of a word while meaning the whole word, as in the saying of the rajiz:

*I said to her, "Stop (qifi)," and she said to me, "Qaf (I stopped)." Do not think we have forgotten the hastening (al-Iyjaf).*

So his saying "Qaf" means "I stopped" (waqaftu). And the saying of another:

*With good, goods; and if evil, then fa... And I do not want evil except that you (ta) will wish.*

He means: "and if evil, then it is evil (fa-sharr), and I do not want evil except that you wish (an tashaa)," so he suffices with the fa and the ta for the rest of the two words.

al-Qurtubi said: and in the hadith, "Whoever helps in the killing of a Muslim with half a word," the hadith... Sufyan said: it is that one says, in "uqtul" (kill), "uq," and beyond what we have mentioned of the views on the openings of the surahs, which are about thirty views.

As for the view which the inductive study of the Qur'an indicates is preponderant, it is this: the disjointed letters are mentioned at the beginnings of the surahs in which they occur as a demonstration of the inimitability of the Qur'an, and that creation is unable to produce its like, even though it is composed of these very disjointed letters with which they converse. al-Razi related this view in his tafsir from al-Mubarrad and a group of verifiers, and al-Qurtubi related it from al-Farra' and Qutrub, and al-Zamakhshari supported it in al-Kashshaf.

Ibn Kathir said: This was the view of the Shaykh, the Imam, the Allamah Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah, and our shaykh, the Hafiz, the mujtahid Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, who related it to me from Ibn Taymiyyah.

The manner in which the inductive study of the Qur'an testifies to this view is that the surahs which begin with the disjointed letters always mention, after the disjointed letters, the defense of the Qur'an and the explanation of its inimitability, and that it is the truth about which there is no doubt.

Mentioning this after them always is an inductive proof that the disjointed letters are intended to show the inimitability of the Qur'an and that it is true.

Allah, Exalted, said in "al-Baqarah": Alif-Lam-Mim [al-Baqarah: 1], and followed that with His saying: ﴿That is the Book, there is no doubt in it﴾. He said in "Al 'Imran": Alif-Lam-Mim [Al 'Imran: 1], and followed that with His saying: ﴿Allah, there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all﴾ ﴿He has sent down to you the Book in truth﴾ the verse [Al 'Imran: 2, 3]. He said in "al-A'raf": Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad [al-A'raf: 1], then said: ﴿A Book sent down to you﴾ the verse [al-A'raf: 2]. He said in Surah Yunus: Alif-Lam-Ra [Yunus: 1], then said: ﴿These are the verses of the wise Book﴾ [Yunus: 1]. He said in this noble surah that we are concerned with, namely Surah Hud: Alif-Lam-Ra [Hud: 1] 30, then said: ﴿A Book whose verses have been made firm, then elaborated, from the presence of One who is All-Wise, All-Aware﴾ [Hud: 1]. He said in Yusuf: Alif-Lam-Ra [Yusuf: 1], then said: ﴿These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ ﴿Indeed We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an﴾ [Yusuf: 1, 2]. He said in al-Ra'd: Alif-Lam-Mim-Ra [al-Ra'd: 1], then said: ﴿These are the verses of the Book, and that which has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth﴾ [al-Ra'd: 1]. He said in Surah Ibrahim: Alif-Lam-Ra [Ibrahim: 1], then said: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you that you may bring mankind out of darknesses into light﴾ the verse [Ibrahim: 1]. He said in al-Hijr: Alif-Lam-Ra [al-Hijr: 1], then said: ﴿These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an﴾. He said in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿Ta-Ha﴾ [Ta-Ha: 1], then said: ﴿We have not sent down the Qur'an to you that you be distressed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 2]. He said in al-Shu'ara': ﴿Ta-Sin-Mim﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 1], then said: ﴿These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief﴾ the verse [al-Shu'ara': 2, 3]. He said in al-Naml: ﴿Ta-Sin﴾ [al-Naml: 2], then said: ﴿These are verses of the Qur'an and a clear Book﴾ [al-Naml: 1]. He said in al-Qasas: ﴿Ta-Sin-Mim﴾ [al-Qasas: 1], then said ﴿These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ ﴿We recite to you some of the news of Musa and Fir'awn﴾ the verse [al-Qasas: 2, 3]. He said in Luqman: Alif-Lam-Mim [Luqman: 3], then said ﴿These are the verses of the wise Book﴾ ﴿A guidance and mercy for the doers of good﴾ [Luqman: 2, 3]. He said in (p-168) "al-Sajdah": Alif-Lam-Mim [al-Sajdah: 1], then said ﴿The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt in it, is from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Sajdah: 2]. He said in "Ya-Sin": ﴿Ya-Sin﴾ [Ya-Sin: 1], then said: ﴿By the wise Qur'an﴾ the verse [Ya-Sin: 2]. He said in "Sad": Sad [Sad: 1], then said: ﴿By the Qur'an full of reminder﴾ the verse [Sad: 1]. He said in Surah al-Mu'min: Ha-Mim [Ghafir: 1], then said ﴿The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾ the verse [Ghafir: 2].

He said in "Fussilat": Ha-Mim [Fussilat: 2], then said ﴿A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ ﴿A Book whose verses are elaborated, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know﴾ the verse [al-Shura: 2, 3]. He said in "al-Shura": ﴿Ha-Mim, 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf﴾ [al-Shura: 1, 2], then said: ﴿Thus does He reveal to you and to those before you﴾ the verse [al-Shura: 3]. He said in "al-Zukhruf": Ha-Mim [al-Zukhruf: 3], then said: ﴿By the clear Book, indeed We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾ the verse [al-Zukhruf: 2, 3]. He said in "al-Dukhan": Ha-Mim [al-Dukhan: 1], then said: ﴿By the clear Book, indeed We sent it down in a blessed night﴾ the verse [al-Dukhan: 2, 3]. He said in "al-Jathiyah": Ha-Mim [al-Jathiyah: 1], then said: ﴿The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ ﴿Indeed in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 2, 3]. He said in "al-Ahqaf": Ha-Mim [al-Ahqaf: 1], then said: ﴿The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth﴾ the verse [al-Ahqaf: 2, 3]. He said in Surah "Qaf": Qaf [Qaf: 1], then said: ﴿By the glorious Qur'an﴾ the verse [Qaf: 1].

We have already presented the discourse of the usulis on the argument from induction, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

We have deferred the discussion of the disjointed letters, although surahs beginning with disjointed letters have already passed, such as al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-A'raf, and Yunus, because the disjointed letters in the Qur'an are mostly Meccan, while al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran are Medinan, and the dominant characteristic governs. We chose Surah Hud to demonstrate this, because its indication of the intended meaning is extremely clear and evident, since His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿A Book whose verses have been made firm, then elaborated, from the presence of One who is All-Wise, All-Aware﴾ [Hud: 1], after His saying: Alif-Lam-Ra [Hud: 1], is very clear regarding what we have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of glad tidings﴾. This noble verse clearly indicates that the great wisdom for which the Qur'an was revealed is that Allah, exalted is He alone, be worshipped, and that nothing be associated with Him in His worship. This is because His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A Book whose verses have been perfected and then detailed from one who is All-Wise, All-Aware﴾ [Hud: 1] ﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾ [Hud: 2], the verse, is explicit that (p-169) the verses of this Book were detailed from the presence of the All-Wise, All-Aware, so that Allah alone be worshipped. This holds whether we say that "an" (أن) is the explanatory particle (al-mufassirah), or that the verbal noun formed from it and its complement is an object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlih). This is because the rule for the explanatory "an" is that what precedes it must contain the meaning of speech, without the letters of speech being present in it.

Its application in this verse is that His saying: ﴿Its verses have been perfected, then detailed﴾ [Hud: 1] contains the meaning of Allah's saying, exalted is He, regarding that perfecting and detailing, without the letters of speech. So the explanation of that is: ﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾.

As for the view that the verbal noun formed from "an" and its complement is an object of purpose, the matter is clear: the meaning of the verse is that the ultimate outcome of the detailing of the Qur'an is that Allah, exalted is He, be worshipped alone, and that nothing be associated with Him. A parallel to this meaning is His saying, exalted is He, in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿Say: It is only revealed to me that your God is but one God; so will you submit?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108]. It is known that the word "innama" (إنما) is one of the forms of restriction (hasr), so it is as if everything that was revealed to him is restricted to the meaning of "There is no god but Allah." We have mentioned in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" that restricting the revelation in this verse of al-Anbiya' to the unity of worship is a restriction of it to its greatest foundation, to which all branches return, because the laws of all the prophets are included within the meaning of "There is no god but Allah," since its meaning is the rejection of all objects of worship other than Allah, exalted is He, in all kinds of worship, and the singling out of Him, exalted is He alone, for all kinds of worship. Thus included in this are all the commands and prohibitions, whether spoken, practical, or doctrinal.

The verses indicating that the sending of the messengers and the revelation of the books were for the sake of Allah being worshipped alone are very numerous, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying]: Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut﴾ [al-Nahl: 36],

• and His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25],

• and His saying: ﴿And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45]

and other verses besides these.

We have pointed to this discussion in "Surat al-Fatihah," and we will, Allah willing, fully explore the discussion of it in "Surat al-Nas," so that it may be a good conclusion to this blessed book.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكم ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إلَيْهِ يُمَتِّعْكم مَتاعًا حَسَنًا إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾ .

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term﴾.

هَذِهِ الآيَةُ الكَرِيمَةُ تَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ الِاسْتِغْفارَ والتَّوْبَةَ إلى اللَّهِ تَعالى مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ سَبَبٌ لِأنْ يُمَتِّعَ اللَّهُ مَن فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ مَتاعًا حَسَنًا إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى؛ لِأنَّهُ رَتَّبَ ذَلِكَ عَلى الِاسْتِغْفارِ والتَّوْبَةِ تَرْتِيبَ الجَزاءِ (p-١٧٠)عَلى شَرْطِهِ.

This noble verse indicates that seeking forgiveness and turning to Allah the Exalted from sins is a cause for Allah to let the one who does so enjoy a good provision until a specified term; because He has ordered that upon seeking forgiveness and repentance in the manner of a consequence upon its condition (p-170).

وthe apparent meaning is that what is intended by the "good provision" is abundance of sustenance, a pleasant life, and well-being in this world, and that what is intended by the "specified term" is death. This is supported by His saying in this noble surah, concerning His Prophet Hud, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace: ﴿And O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance; He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain and increase you in strength upon your strength﴾ [Hud: 52]; and His saying concerning "Nuh" (Noah): ﴿So I said, "Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed, He is ever Forgiving. He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain and provide you with wealth and sons and make for you gardens and make for you rivers"﴾ [Nuh: 10–12]; and His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [An-Nahl: 97], and so on; and His saying: ﴿And if the people of the cities had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth﴾ [Al-A'raf: 96]; and His saying: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 66]; and His saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [At-Talaq: 2–3]; in addition to other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their breasts to hide from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾.

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, makes clear that nothing is hidden from Him, and that the secret is like the open before Him. He is Knowing of what the inner hearts harbor, and of what is made public and what is kept private. The verses that clarify this are very numerous.

• Such as His saying: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than his jugular vein﴾ [Qaf: 16],

• And His saying, majestic and exalted: ﴿And know that Allah knows what is within your souls, so beware of Him﴾

• And His saying: ﴿Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent﴾ [al-A'raf: 7],

• And His saying: ﴿And you are not in any matter or recite from it of the Qur'an or do any deed except that We are witness over you when you are involved in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven﴾ [Yunus: 61], and so on.

And you will not turn a page of the noble Mushaf without finding in it a verse with this meaning.

An important admonition

Know that Allah, blessed and exalted, has not sent down from the heaven to the earth a greater admonisher, nor a more mighty restrainer, than what these noble verses and their like in the Qur'an contain: that He, exalted is He, is Knowing of everything His creation does, Watchful over them, not absent from what they do. The scholars have coined for this greatest admonisher and mightiest restrainer an example, so that it becomes like something perceptible. They said: Suppose that a king who slays men, sheds blood, and is severe in seizing and punishing those who violate his sanctity unjustly, with his executioner standing at his head, the leather mat spread out for killing, and the sword dripping blood, and around this king, who has such a description, are his concubines, wives and daughters. Do you think that any of those present would intend an illicit act or a forbidden thing with the king's daughters or wives while he is looking at him, knowing that he is watching him?! No, by no means! Rather, all those present would be fearful, their hearts trembling, their eyes humbled, their limbs still, out of fear of that king's assault.

And there is no doubt, "and to Allah belongs the highest example," that the Lord of the heavens and the earth, majestic and exalted, is more knowing, more watchful, mightier in seizing, and more severe in punishment than that king, and His sanctuary on His earth is His prohibitions. So when the weak human notices that his Lord, majestic and exalted, is not absent from him, and that He is aware of everything he says, does, and intends, his heart softens, he fears Allah, the Exalted, and perfects his deed for Allah, majestic and exalted.

Among the secrets of this great admonition is that Allah, blessed and exalted, declared that the wisdom for which He created creation is that He may test them: which of them is best in deed. He did not say: which of them is most in deed. So the testing is in excellence of deed, as He, exalted is He, said in this noble surah: ﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, while His Throne was upon the water, that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [Hud: 7].

And He said in Surah al-Mulk: ﴿He who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving﴾ [al-Mulk: 2].

And there is no doubt that the intelligent person, when he knows that the wisdom for which he was created is that he be tested, that is, examined in excellence of deed, will be concerned with the utmost concern about the means that lead to his success in this examination. For this great wisdom, Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ about this, so that he might teach it to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and said: "Inform me about ihsan (excellence)," meaning: and that is what creation was created for, the testing in it. The Prophet ﷺ then explained that the path to that is this admonition and the greatest restrainer, which is watchfulness of Allah, the Exalted, and knowledge that nothing of what His creation does is hidden from Him. So he said to him: "Ihsan is that you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you."

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their breasts﴾ [Hud: 5], and His saying: ﴿they cover themselves with their garments﴾ [Hud: 5], and regarding the referent of the pronoun in His saying: "from Him" [Hud: 5].

Some scholars said: the meaning of ﴿they fold their breasts﴾ [Hud: 5] is that they turn away from the truth and deviate from it, because whoever faces something confronts it with his chest, and whoever turns away from it and deviates bends his breast away from it and turns his side away from it. Al-Zamakhshari explained it thus in al-Kashshaf.

The compiler of this work, may Allah forgive him, said: This meaning is well known in the speech of the Arabs. They express by the crookedness of the chest the turning away from something and inclining away from it, and they express by the straightening of the chest the intention toward something and not inclining away from it.

From the first is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah Ghaylan ibn 'Uqbah al-'Adawi, 'Adiyy al-Rababi:

O my two companions, bend, may Allah bless you both, toward the abode of Mayy from the breasts of the mounts.

May there be a bend by which Allah repays you both with Him, the reward, or the covenant of a companion is fulfilled.

He means: turn the breasts of the mounts toward the abode of Mayy.

From the second is the saying of al-Shanfara:

Keep, O sons of my mother, the breasts of your mounts [facing], for I am inclined toward a people other than you.

And the saying of another:

I say to Umm Zinba', "Keep straight," the breasts of life toward the side of Banu Tamim.

It was also said: this noble verse was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shuraiq al-Thaqafi, ally of Banu Zuhrah.

He was sweet of speech, meeting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with what he loved, while concealing in his heart what displeased him.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning some of the hypocrites, who, when he passed by the Prophet ﷺ, would fold his chest and back, lower his head and cover his face, so that the Prophet ﷺ would not see him and call him to faith. This meaning is related from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad.

And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that it was revealed concerning a people who disliked to have intercourse or relieve themselves while there was no barrier between them and the heaven, being shy before Allah.

Some scholars said: the meaning of ﴿they cover themselves with their garments﴾ [Hud: 5] is that they cover their heads out of their dislike of hearing the speech of Allah, like His saying, exalted is He, about Nuh: ﴿And indeed, every time I called them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their garments﴾ [Nuh: 7], and the verse.

It was also said: when they committed evil, they would fold their breasts and cover their heads, thinking that if they did that they would hide their deed from Allah, majestic and exalted. This interpretation is supported by His saying: ﴿that they may hide from Him﴾ [Hud: 5], and the verse.

Ibn 'Abbas recited this noble verse: "Unquestionably, their breasts fold [تَثْنَوْنِي]..." [Hud: 5], where tathnawni is the present tense of ithnawna, its pattern being if'awala from al-thany, just as one says ihlawla from al-halawah. The word ṣudūruhum in Ibn 'Abbas's reading is in the nominative as the subject of tathnawni. The pronoun in His saying "from Him" refers, according to the more apparent of the two opinions, to Allah, exalted is He; and it was said that it refers to him ﷺ, as has passed in the sayings on the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was over the water, that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾. In this noble verse He declares explicitly that He created the heavens and the earth for the wisdom of testing the creation, and He did not create them in vain or for nothing. He declared Himself exalted above that, and He declared that whoever supposes such is among those who disbelieve, and He threatened them with the Fire. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad: 27]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ ﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115, 116]. He said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56], and He said: ﴿He who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [al-Mulk: 2], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if We defer the punishment from them until a specified community (ummah)﴾ [the verse], the meaning of "ummah" here is a period of time. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the one who was saved of the two and remembered after a period (ummah)﴾, i.e., he remembered after a span of time.

Reminder

The word "ummah" (community, nation; a group bound by a common religion or path) is used in the Qur'an in four ways:

The first: its use for a span or period of time, which is what we mentioned here.

The second: its use for a group of people, which is the most common usage,

• as in His saying, ﴿He found upon it a community (ummah) of people watering﴾ [al-Qasas: 23],

• and His saying: ﴿And for every community (ummah) there is a messenger﴾ [Yunus: 47],

• and His saying: ﴿Mankind were one community (ummah)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213],

and beyond that from the verses.

The third: its use for a man who is taken as a leader and exemplar, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a community (ummah)﴾ [al-Nahl: 120].

The fourth: its use for religious law and way of life, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (ummah)﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 22], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community (ummah)﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 52], and beyond that from the verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 15:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted has explicitly stated that whoever does a deed intending by it the life of this world, He gives him the reward of his deed in this world, and there is nothing for him in the Hereafter except the Fire.

A parallel to this verse is His saying in Surat ash-Shura: ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it, and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ [ash-Shura: 20]. However, He clarifies in Surat Bani Isra'il that this is conditioned upon His will, Mighty and Exalted is He, in His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We desire﴾ — the verse [al-Isra': 18]. We have clarified this matter to the utmost clarity in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" in the discussion of this noble verse, and therefore we have abbreviated it here.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-301) In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surat Hud

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein.﴾

This noble verse explicitly states that the disbeliever is recompensed for his good deeds, such as charity, maintaining kinship ties, hospitality to guests, and relieving the distressed, in this world only and not in the Hereafter, because He, the Exalted, said: ﴿We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾, meaning the life of this world. Then He stated their nullification in the Hereafter by His saying: ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and what they did therein becomes void﴾ — the verse [Hud: 16].

A parallel to this verse is His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth, and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it﴾ — the verse [ash-Shura: 20], and His saying: ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire: "You have used up your good things in your worldly life"﴾ — the verse [al-Ahqaf: 20].

According to what Ibn Zayd said, and His saying: ﴿And He found Allah with him, and He paid him his account in full﴾ [an-Nur: 39], according to one of the two opinions, and His saying: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ [al-Anfal: 33], according to one of the previously mentioned opinions in Surat al-Anfal. It has been authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ that "the disbeliever is recompensed for his good deeds in this world." Yet there are other verses indicating the nullification of the disbeliever's deeds and their complete annulment at the root, and in some of them is the explicit statement of their nullification in this world and the Hereafter together, in the case of apostasy and in other cases.

As for the verses indicating their nullification at the root, they include His saying: ﴿Their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows hard on a stormy day﴾ [Ibrahim: 18], and His saying: ﴿Their deeds are like a mirage﴾ — the verse [an-Nur: 39], and His saying: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23].

As for the verses indicating their nullification in this world together with the Hereafter, they include His saying concerning the disbelief of the apostate: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever — those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾ (p-302) [al-Baqarah: 217], and His saying concerning the disbelief of one who is not an apostate: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah⁠ — to His saying — ﴿those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 22]. Allah the Exalted has also made clear in other verses that the bounty bestowed upon them in this world is not for honor but for gradual enticement and destruction.

- Like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We will lead them step by step from where they do not know﴾ ﴿And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾ [al-A'raf: 182–183],

- And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 178],

- And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the doors of every thing until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair﴾ [al-An'am: 44],

- And His saying: ﴿Do they think that what We supply them with of wealth and children⁠ ⁠— ⁠We hasten to them with good things? Rather, they do not perceive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 55–56],

- And His saying: ﴿Say: Whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension﴾ [Maryam: 75],

- And His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one nation⁠ — to His saying — and the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 33–35],

and other verses besides these.

The answer comes in four aspects:

First: and its correctness appears to me because of the apparent indication of the Qur'an, that among the disbelievers is one whom Allah rewards for his deed in this world, as indicated by verses and confirmed by a hadith, and among them is one whom He does not reward in this world, as indicated by other verses. This is witnessed among them in this world: among them is one who is in comfortable living, and among them is one who is in hardship and constriction.

The way the Qur'an indicates this is that He, the Exalted, pointed to it by specifying it with the will in His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We desire﴾ [al-Isra': 18].

So it specifies the generality of His saying: ﴿We will pay them in full for their deeds﴾ [Hud: 15], and the generality of His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it﴾ [ash-Shura: 20].

Among those who explicitly stated that it specifies both of them is the Hafiz Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari, in the Book of ar-Riqaq, in the discussion of al-Bukhari's chapter heading "Chapter: The abundant ones are the poor ones" and His saying, the Exalted: (p-303) ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment⁠ — the two verses.

This specification is also supported by His saying about some of the disbelievers: ﴿They have lost this world and the Hereafter; that is the manifest loss﴾ [al-Hajj: 11].

The majority of scholars hold that the general is to be read in light of the specific and the absolute in light of the restricted, as is established in the principles of jurisprudence.

Second: and this is also a sound view, that the disbeliever is rewarded for his deed with health, abundance of provision, children, and the like, as Allah the Exalted explicitly said: ﴿We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾, meaning this world, and He emphasized this by His saying: ﴿and they will not be deprived therein﴾, and by its apparent and immediate meaning as we have mentioned.

Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah and ad-Dahhak interpreted it so, as Ibn Jarir transmitted from them. On this view, the nullification of their deeds in this world means that they are not taken into account legally in protecting blood, inheritance, marriage, or other matters, and the gates of heaven are not opened for them, and they do not ascend to Allah the Exalted, by the proof of His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]; and they are not stored up for them in beneficial deeds, nor are they in the record of the righteous in 'Illiyyin. And this suffices as nullification.

As for the mere worldly benefit they gain from them, it is in Allah's sight as nothing, and so it does not contradict their nullification, by the proof of His saying: ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but enjoyment﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 185],

and His saying: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play; and indeed, the Final Abode—that is the (true) life, if they only knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64],

and His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one nation⁠ — to His saying — for the righteous﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 33–35]. The verses on this matter are numerous.

Among what clarifies this meaning is the hadith: "If the world weighed with Allah the wing of a mosquito, He would not give a disbeliever a sip of water from it."

Ibn Kathir mentioned this hadith in his interpretation of His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one nation⁠ — the verses.

(p-304) Then he said: al-Baghawi transmitted it with a chain through Zakariyya ibn Manzur, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned it.

And at-Tabarani narrated it through the route of Zam'ah ibn Salih, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from the Prophet ﷺ: "If the world were equal with Allah to the wing of a mosquito, He would not give a disbeliever anything of it."

The author, its annotator, may Allah pardon him, says: It is not hidden that the intent of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, in what we have quoted from him is that both routes are weak, but each of them is strengthened by the other, so the collection is fit for argument, as is established in the science of hadith, that weak routes which are considered may reinforce one another and thus become fit for argument.

"Do not contend with one who is among a household; two weak ones may overcome a strong one."

This is because Zakariyya ibn Manzur ibn Tha'labah al-Qurazi and Zam'ah ibn Salih al-Janadi are both weak. Muslim narrated from Zam'ah only in conjunction with others, not independently in narration, as Ibn Hajar explained in at-Taqrib.

Third: the meaning of ﴿We will pay them in full for their deeds﴾ is that We give them the aim for which they worked in this world, like one who fought so that it might be said "he is brave," one who recited so that it might be said "he is a reciter," and one who gave charity so that it might be said "he is generous." It has been said to them, and this is what is meant by paying them in full for their deeds on this interpretation.

This is supported by the hadith narrated by Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet, concerning the warrior, the reciter, and the giver of charity, that it will be said to each of them: "You did it so that it would be said, and it has been said." It was recorded by at-Tirmidhi in an extended form, and its origin is in Muslim, as Ibn Hajar said, and Ibn Jarir also narrated it. Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, cited as evidence for the authenticity of this hadith of Abu Hurayrah His saying: ﴿We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾, and this is an interpretation from him, may Allah be pleased with him, of this verse in a way that supports this third aspect.

Fourth: the intended meaning of the verse is the hypocrites who go out for jihad not seeking the Face of Allah, but seeking the spoils. They are given their share of them in this world, and they have no share in their jihad in the Hereafter. The giving of their share from them is the paying of their deeds in full according to this view, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his appointed place﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, declares explicitly that no one disbelieves in this Qur'an, whoever he may be, except that he enters the Fire. This is explicit evidence of the universality of the message of our Prophet ﷺ to all of creation. The verses indicating this are numerous, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it and whomever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19],

• And His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1],

• And His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ etc. [Saba': 28],

• And His saying: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ etc. [al-A'raf: 158].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not be in doubt about it; indeed, it is the truth from your Lord﴾ etc. In this noble verse, Allah, exalted and majestic is He, forbids doubt about this great Qur'an, and declares that it is the truth from Allah. The verses clarifying this meaning are very numerous, such as His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book about which there is no doubt﴾ etc. [al-Baqarah: 1-2], and His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The revelation of the Book, about which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds﴾, and similar verses. And al-miryah (المِرْيَة) means doubt.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, declares explicitly that most people do not believe (p-175), and He explains this also in many places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you strive eagerly, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103],

• And His saying: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you﴾ [al-An'am: 116],

• And His saying: ﴿And most of the former peoples had already gone astray before them﴾ [al-Saffat: 71],

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 8, 67, 103, 121],

and other verses besides these.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for them﴾ and the rest of the verse. In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, explains that the disbelievers who turn people away from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked will have the punishment doubled for them on the Day of Resurrection, because they are punished for their own misguidance and are also punished for misguiding others, as He clarified in His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve and turn away from the way of Allah — We will increase their punishment upon punishment for what they used to spread of corruption﴾ [An-Nahl: 88].

He also explained in another place that the punishment is doubled for both the followers and the leaders, in His saying in al-A'raf: ﴿Until, when they have all gathered therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know"﴾ and the rest of the verse [Al-A'raf: 38].

As for His saying: ﴿They were not able to hear, nor did they used to see﴾, the scholars have several interpretations of this noble verse, some of which are supported by the Qur'an:

The first, which is the choice of Ibn Jarir al-Tabari (al-Tabari) in his tafsir, and which he transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah: the meaning of ﴿They were not able to hear﴾ and the rest of the verse [Hud: 20] is that they are not able to hear the truth in a way that benefits them, nor to see it with the sight of one who is guided, because they were occupied with the disbelief in which they remained, neglecting the use of their faculties in obedience to Allah, exalted is He, although they did have hearing and sight.

What supports this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had given them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and their sight and their hearts did not avail them anything, since they used to deny the signs of Allah﴾ and the rest of the verse [Al-Ahqaf: 26].

The second, which is the most apparent to me: the inability mentioned in the verse is only due to the seal that Allah set upon their hearts and their hearing, and the veil that He placed over their sight.

What supports this view is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their sight is a veil﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 7], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾, and similar verses.

That sealing and those coverings upon the hearts are a recompense from Allah, exalted is He, for them, because of their hastening to disbelief and denial of the messengers by their own choice and will, as many verses indicate,

such as His saying: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed their hearts because of their disbelief﴾ [An-Nisa': 155],

and His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [As-Saff: 5],

and His saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ and the rest of the verse [Al-Baqarah: 10],

and His saying: ﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to their filth upon their filth﴾ and the rest of the verse [At-Tawbah: 125],

and His saying: ﴿And We will turn their hearts and their sight away, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ and the rest of the verse [Al-An'am: 110],

along with other verses besides these.

The third: the meaning is: they were not able to hear, that is, because of the intensity of their aversion to the speech of the messengers, following the custom of the Arabs in saying, "I cannot hear such-and-such," when someone is extremely averse to it and hates it. What supports this view is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you will recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve the denial; they almost attack those who recite to them Our verses﴾ [Al-Hajj: 72], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an"﴾ and the rest of the verse [Fussilat: 26], and His saying: ﴿And indeed, whenever I call them, that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears﴾.

The fourth: that "ma" (what) is a temporal verbal particle (ma masdariyya zarfiyya), meaning: the punishment is doubled for them for the duration of their being able to hear and to see, that is, the punishment is doubled for them continually.

The fifth: that "ma" is a verbal particle in a position of accusative case through the elision of the governing preposition (naza' al-khafid), meaning: the punishment is doubled for them because they were able to hear and to see in the abode of this world, yet they abandoned the truth although they were able to perceive it with their hearing and sight. We have already mentioned in Surat An-Nisa' the view of al-Akhfash al-Asghar (the Younger al-Akhfash) that the accusative case through the elision of the governing preposition is analogically valid in every case when there is no risk of ambiguity.

The sixth: that His saying: ﴿They were not able to hear, nor did they used to see﴾ [Hud: 20] describes the idols that they took as allies besides Allah. In that case it is connected to His saying: ﴿And they had no allies besides Allah﴾ [Hud: 20], and the clause ﴿The punishment will be doubled for them﴾ [Hud: 20] is parenthetical. The meaning according to this view is: "And they had no allies besides Allah, who were not able to hear nor to see," that is, the idols that they took as allies besides Allah. Whatever does not hear and does not see cannot rightly be an ally to anyone.

What supports the meaning of this view is His saying, exalted is He, in Al-A'raf: ﴿Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾ and the rest of the verse [Al-A'raf: 195], and similar verses.

We have already mentioned in the interpretation of this blessed book that a noble verse may have several opinions, all of which are supported by a Qur'an verse, so we mention all of them, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He. (p-177)

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The likeness of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing﴾, the verse.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, set forth the likeness of the disbeliever as the blind and the deaf, and set forth the likeness of the believer as the hearing and the seeing. He made clear that the two are not equal, nor are the blind and the seeing equal, nor are the deaf and the hearing equal. He clarified this meaning in many verses:

His saying: ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal﴾ ﴿nor are the darknesses and the light﴾ ﴿nor the shade and the heat﴾ ﴿nor are the living and the dead equal. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, and you cannot make hear those who are in the graves. You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir: 19-23].

And His saying: ﴿Is then one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾, the verse [al-Ra'd: 19].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating﴾ [al-Naml: 80], and other verses to this effect.

The commentary of Allah says in this noble verse: that the chieftains (al-Mala', the leading notables) of the people of Nuh said to him: "We do not see that those who follow you from among us are anyone but the lowest and the basest," and He mentioned in Surat al-Shu'ara' that following the lowly was, in their view, a barrier preventing them from following him, in His saying: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you while the lowest have followed you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111].

And in this noble surah He made clear that Nuh, upon him and upon our Prophet be peace, refused to drive away those believers who had followed him, in His saying: ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾ ﴿And O my people, who would support me against Allah if I drove them away?﴾ [Hud: 29, 30] and the verse. He also mentioned that from him in al-Shu'ara' with His saying: ﴿Their account is only with my Lord, if you could perceive. And I will not drive away the believers﴾.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 28:

Allah's statement: ﴿He said: "O my people, tell me, if I am upon a clear proof from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself, but it has been concealed from you, shall we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?"﴾

In this noble verse, Allah mentions about His Prophet Noah that he said to his people: "Tell me" (ara'aytum) [Hud: 28], i.e., inform me. ﴿If I am upon a clear proof from my Lord﴾ [Hud: 28], i.e., upon certainty and a true prophethood with no doubt in it, and He has given me mercy from Himself, namely what He revealed to me of monotheism (tawhid) and guidance, so all of that has been hidden from you and you have not believed it to be true. Can I compel you to it and force your hearts to submit and yield to that clear proof with which Allah has graciously favoured me and shown me mercy by bestowing it, while you are averse to it? That is, the guidance of your hearts is not in my hand, even if it is manifest and clear without any ambiguity, if Allah, Mighty and Exalted, does not guide you to it.

Allah, Mighty and Exalted, also expressed this meaning concerning Noah in this noble surah, in His saying: ﴿And my counsel will not benefit you if I wish to counsel you, if Allah wills to lead you astray; He is your Lord﴾ [Hud: 34], to the end of the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return for it. My reward is only from Allah﴾, to the end of the verse.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, mentions about His Prophet Nuh, peace and blessings be upon him and upon our Prophet: that he informed his people that he does not ask them for wealth in exchange for what he brought them of revelation and guidance; rather, he gives them that great good freely, without taking any wage in return for it.

He explains in many verses that this is the way of the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, such as His saying in Surat Saba' about our Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say, "Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is for you. My reward is only from Allah"﴾ to the end of the verse [Saba': 47].

And His saying in the same surah, at the end of Surat Sad: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it, nor am I of those who pretend."﴾ [Sad: 86].

And His saying in at-Tur and al-Qalam: ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ [at-Tur: 40] [68:46].

And His saying in al-Furqan: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it, except that whoever wills may take to his Lord a way."﴾ [al-Furqan: 57].

And His saying in al-An'am: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for a reward for it; it is only a reminder to the worlds."﴾ [al-An'am: 90].

And His saying about Hud in Surat Hud: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for a reward for it. My reward is only from the One who originated me﴾ to the end of the verse [Hud: 51].

And His saying in ash-Shu'ara' about Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb, upon them and upon our Prophet be peace: ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 109].

And His saying, exalted is He, about the messengers of the town mentioned in Surat Ya-Sin: ﴿Follow the messengers﴾ ﴿Follow those who do not ask you for a reward﴾ to the end of the verse [Ya-Sin: 20, 21].

We have already explained the way of reconciling these mentioned verses with His saying, exalted is He: (p-179) ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it, except affection among relatives."﴾ in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" in Surat Saba', in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say, "Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is for you."﴾ [Saba': 47].

From these noble verses it is derived that it is obligatory upon the followers of the Messengers, from among the scholars and others, to give freely what knowledge they have, without taking any compensation for it, and that it is not appropriate to take a wage for teaching the Book of Allah, exalted is He, nor for teaching beliefs (al-'aqa'id) and the lawful and the unlawful (al-halal wa al-haram).

This is reinforced by hadiths that indicate the same meaning. Among them is what Ibn Majah, al-Bayhaqi, and al-Ruwayani in his Musnad narrated, "from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I taught a man the Qur'an, and he gifted me a bow. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: 'If you take it, you have taken a bow of fire,' so I returned it."

Al-Bayhaqi and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said regarding this hadith: it is munqati' (disconnected), namely between 'Atiyyah al-Kala'i and Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Al-Mizzi also said likewise.

Ibn Hajar criticized this, saying that 'Atiyyah was born during the time of the Prophet ﷺ.

Ibn al-Qattan gave it a defect, saying that its narrator from the aforementioned 'Atiyyah is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salm, who is unknown (majhul).

Ibn Hajar also said of him in at-Taqrib: Shami, majhul.

Al-Shawkani said in Nayl al-Awtar: "It has chains from Ubayy." Ibn al-Qattan said: "Nothing from them is established." The Hafiz said: "In what he said there is room for consideration."

Al-Mizzi in al-Atraf mentioned for it several chains, among them that the one who taught him was Ubayy, namely al-Tufayl ibn 'Amr, and what supports it is what al-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat "from al-Tufayl ibn 'Amr al-Dawsi who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b taught me the Qur'an, so I gave him a bow as a gift. He went to the Prophet ﷺ wearing it on his neck, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Wear it from Jahannam'," the hadith. Al-Shawkani also said: "And on this topic, from Mu'adh in al-Hakim and al-Bazzar, similar to the hadith of Ubayy, and from Abu al-Darda' in al-Darimi with a chain meeting the condition of Muslim, similarly."

Among them is what Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated, "from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I taught some people of the Suffah the Book and the Qur'an, and a man from among them gifted me a bow. I said: It is not wealth, and I will shoot with it in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. I will certainly come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him. So I came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, a man, one of those I taught the Book and the Qur'an, gifted me a bow; it is not wealth, and I will shoot with it in the way of Allah. He said: 'If you wish to be collared with a collar of fire, then accept it.'" In its chain is al-Mughirah ibn Ziyad al-Mawsili. Al-Shawkani said: Waki' and Yahya ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy, and a group spoke about him.

(p-180) Imam Ahmad said: "He is weak in hadith; he narrated munkar hadiths, and every hadith he raised (to the Prophet) is munkar." Abu Zur'ah al-Razi said: "His hadith is not to be used as evidence." End of quote. Ibn Hajar also said of him in at-Taqrib: al-Mughirah ibn Ziyad al-Bajali, Abu Hisham or Hashim, al-Mawsili, is truthful (saduq) but has errors. This hadith was narrated by Abu Dawud through another route which does not include the aforementioned al-Mughirah: 'Amr ibn 'Uthman and Kathir ibn 'Ubayd told us, both said: Baqiyyah told us, Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bashshar told me; 'Amr said: and 'Ubadah ibn Nusayy told me, from Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, similar to this report, and the first is more complete. I said: What do you think about it, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "A burning coal between your shoulders that you wear" or "that you hang on yourself." End of quote in his words. In the chain of this narration is Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid, about whom a group has spoken, while others have declared him trustworthy when he narrates from trustworthy narrators; he is one of the men of Muslim, and al-Bukhari narrated from him in suspended form (ta'liq).

Ibn Hajar said of him in at-Taqrib: truthful, but he frequently practiced tadlis (concealment) from weak narrators. The apparent view is that the most balanced of the opinions about him is that if he explicitly states hearing from trustworthy narrators, there is no harm in it; and this hadith of his is reinforced by what has preceded and what will come, if Allah, exalted is He, wills.

Among them is what Imam Ahmad and at-Tirmidhi narrated from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with both of them, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Recite the Qur'an and ask Allah by it, for after you there will be a people who recite the Qur'an and ask people by it." At-Tirmidhi said regarding this hadith: its chain is not so.

Among them is what Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan: Wahb ibn Baqiyyah told us, Khalid informed us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were reciting the Qur'an, and among us were the Bedouin and the non-Arab. He said: 'Recite, for each of you is good, and there will come people who straighten it as an arrow is straightened, hastening its reward and not deferring it.'" Ahmad ibn Salih told us, 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb told us, 'Umar and Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Bakr ibn Sawadah, from Wafa' ibn Shurayh al-Sadafi, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were contending (over the Qur'an), and he said: 'Praise be to Allah. The Book of Allah is one, and among you are the red, the white, and the black. Recite before there come people who straighten it as the arrow is straightened, hastening its reward and not deferring it.'" End of quote.

Among them is what Imam Ahmad narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shibl, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Recite the Qur'an, and do not exaggerate in it, nor turn away from it, nor eat by it, nor make much of it by it." Al-Shawkani, may Allah have mercy on him, said in Nayl al-Awtar regarding this hadith: In Majma' al-Zawa'id it is said: the men of Ahmad are trustworthy.

Among them is what al-Athram narrated in his Sunan from Ubayy, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I used to visit a elderly man who had been afflicted with an illness and confined to his house, and I would recite the Qur'an to him. He would be brought food, the like of which I did not eat in Madinah, (p-181) and something troubled my soul, so I mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: 'If that food is his food and the food of his family, then eat of it; but if he is presenting it to you as a gift, then do not eat it.'" End of quote, through the transmission of Ibn Qudamah in al-Mughni and al-Shawkani in Nayl al-Awtar.

These proofs and the like indicate that it is not permissible to take a wage for teaching the Qur'an and religious matters.

Among those who held this view: Imam Ahmad in one of the two narrations, Abu Hanifah, al-Dahhak ibn Qays, and 'Ata'.

Al-Zuhri and Ishaq disliked teaching the Qur'an for pay.

'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq said: "These loaves which teachers take are unlawful earnings (suht)."

Among those who disliked a teacher's wage when made a condition: al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Tawus, al-Sha'bi, and al-Nakha'i, as stated in al-Mughni, and it said: the apparent meaning of Imam Ahmad's words is the permissibility of the teacher taking what is given to him without condition.

Most of the people of knowledge went to the permissibility of taking a wage for teaching the Qur'an, and this is the position of Malik and al-Shafi'i.

Among those who permitted teachers' wages: Abu Qilabah, Abu Thawr, and Ibn al-Mundhir.

Abu Talib transmitted from Ahmad that he said: "Teaching is more beloved to me than to be entrusted to these sultans, or to be entrusted to a man from the common people for an estate, or than to borrow and trade, perhaps he will not be able to repay and will meet Allah, exalted is He, with people's trusts. Teaching is more beloved to me."

This indicates that his prohibition in the place where he prohibited it is for reprehensibility (karahah), not for prohibition (tahrim), as stated by Ibn Qudamah in al-Mughni.

The proponents of this view argued with evidences, among them what the two Shaykhs and others narrated from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him: "A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have given myself to you. She stood for a long time. A man stood and said: O Messenger of Allah, marry her to me if you have no need of her. He ﷺ said: 'Do you have anything to give her as a dowry?' He said: I have nothing but my waist-wrapper. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'If you give her your waist-wrapper, you will sit without a waist-wrapper, so seek something.' He said: I find nothing. He said: 'Seek even an iron ring.' He sought but found nothing. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Do you have anything of the Qur'an?' He said: Yes, such and such surah, naming them. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'I have married her to you for what you have of the Qur'an.'" In another narration: "I have made her yours (mallaktukaha) for what you have of the Qur'an." They said: this man, the Prophet ﷺ permitted him to make his teaching of part of the Qur'an to this woman a substitute for her dowry, and it is explicit that compensation for teaching the Qur'an is permissible. As for what some scholars answered in reply to using this hadith as evidence, that he ﷺ married him to her without a dowry out of honor to him for memorizing that amount of the Qur'an, and did not make the teaching a dowry for her, it is rejected by what is established in some narrations in Sahih Muslim, that he ﷺ said: "Go, I have married her to you, so teach her from the Qur'an." And in a narration of Abu Dawud: "Teach her twenty verses, and she is your wife."

They also argued with the general wording of his saying ﷺ, established in Sahih al-Bukhari from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: "The most deserving of what you take a wage for is the Book of Allah." They said: although the hadith came concerning a reward for ruqyah with the Book of Allah, the consideration is with the generality of the wording, not the specific cause; and the possibility of distinguishing between a reward for ruqyah and a wage for teaching is evident.

The compiler of these notes, may Allah forgive him, says: What appears to me, and Allah, exalted is He, knows best, is that the person, if he is not driven by urgent necessity, it is better for him not to take compensation for teaching the Qur'an, the beliefs, and the lawful and unlawful, due to the evidences mentioned earlier. If necessity drives him, he may take only to the extent of need from the public treasury of the Muslims, because what is taken from the treasury apparently falls under assistance in carrying out teaching, not under wage.

And it is better for one whom Allah has made independent to abstain from taking anything in return for teaching the Qur'an, the beliefs, and the lawful and unlawful. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We said: "Carry in it two of each kind, a pair"﴾, the verse. In this noble verse, God, majestic and exalted, mentioned that He commanded His prophet Noah, upon him and upon our Prophet be blessings and peace, to carry in his ship two of each kind, a pair. In the surah ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ He clarified that He commanded him to make them enter it (yaslukahum), i.e., to cause them to enter it.

This indicates that the ship contains compartments into which the passengers enter. That is in His saying: ﴿Then when Our command comes and the oven overflows, insert into it two of each kind, a pair﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 27]. The meaning of usluk is: enter into it two of each kind, a pair. The Arabs say: "salaktu al-shay' fi al-shay'" (I inserted the thing into the thing), meaning "adkhaltuhu fihi" (I made it enter into it). There is another dialect for this, which is "aslaktuhu fihi" in the quadriliteral form on the pattern af'ala, while the triliteral form (salaka) is the language of the Qur'an,

such as:

• His saying: ﴿So insert into it two of each kind, a pair﴾, the verse [al-Mu'minun: 27];

• His saying: ﴿Insert your hand into your pocket﴾, the verse [al-Qasas: 32];

• His saying: ﴿Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾, the verse [al-Shu'ara': 200];

• His saying: (p-183) ﴿Thus We cause it to enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾, the verse [al-Hijr: 12];

• His saying: ﴿What has caused you to enter Saqar?﴾, the verse [al-Muddaththir: 42].

From this is the saying of the poet:

"And I was the strong opponent of your adversary, not counting him,
And they made you enter (saluka) on a day of hardship."

From the quadriliteral form is the saying of Abd Manaf ibn Rub' al-Hudhali:

"Until, when they made them enter (aslakuhum) into a narrow place,
Driving them in a rush, as the camel drivers drive the scattered camels."

The one who annotates this work, may God pardon him, says: What appears to me is that the origin of the word salk, which is the thread, is a verb in the sense of a passive participle, like dhibh in the sense of madhbuh (slaughtered) and qitl in the sense of maqtul (killed), because the thread passes through (yaslukuh, i.e., enters) the beads in order to string them together, as al-Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami said:

"An eye whose sorrow has made it sleepless,
Water floods it at times and flows down.

It is as if it were a string of pearls in the hand of one who strings them,
Its thread has broken, so it is scattered."

And God knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except for those against whom the word has already preceded﴾, the verse. In this noble verse, God, majestic and exalted, mentioned that He commanded Noah to carry his family in the ship, except for those against whom the word had already preceded, i.e., against whom the word had already gone forth from God that he is wretched and that he will perish with the disbelievers.

He did not specify here who among them the word had preceded against, but after this He clarified that the one against whom the word had preceded from his family was his son and his wife.

Concerning his son against whom the word had preceded, He said: ﴿And Noah called to his son, who was apart, "O my son, ride with us and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾ up to His saying ﴿And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned﴾ [Hud: 42-43]. He also said concerning him: ﴿He said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one of] unrighteous conduct."﴾, the verse [Hud: 46]. And concerning his wife He said: ﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah﴾ up to His saying ﴿"Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he said, "Embark therein; in the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted mentions that His prophet Nuh (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, the prayer and peace) commanded those of his companions about whom it was said to him, "Carry them therein," that they should board it, saying: ﴿In the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring﴾ [Hud: 41]. That is: in the name of Allah is its running upon the surface of the water, and in the name of Allah is the end of its course, which is its mooring (rusuww).

And He explained in "Surat al-Falah" (the Surah of Success, i.e. al-Mu'minun) that when he and those with him settled into the ship, he commanded them to praise (p-184) Allah, who saved them from the disbelieving wrongdoers, and to ask Him to bring them down to a blessed landing place. This is in His saying: ﴿So when you and those with you are settled upon the ship, say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people." And say, "My Lord, let me land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best of those who bring to land."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 28, 29].

And He explained in "Surat al-Zukhruf" what should be said when boarding ships and other vehicles, in His saying: ﴿And who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride, that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you are seated upon them and say, "Exalted is He who has subjected these to us, and we were not capable of that. And indeed, to our Lord we will return."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 12-14]. The meaning of His saying "muqrinin" is "capable" (mutiqin). From it is the saying of 'Amr ibn Ma'd Yakrib:

"The tribes certainly know that 'Aqil, for us, in calamities, is not incapable of us (bi-muqrinina)."

And the saying of another:

"You have mounted two restive, cowardly beasts, and you are not capable (bi-muqrinina) of taming the untamed."

And the saying of Ibn Harmah:

"And it has borne what carried me, and little is it that endurance of rejection can be borne, O Da'd, and of abandonment."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 42:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains﴾ – the verse.

Allah, exalted is He, mentions in this noble verse that the ship sailed with Noah and those with him over a great body of water whose waves are like mountains.

He explained its sailing upon that tremendous water in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing vessel﴾ ﴿That We might make it for you a reminder and that a conscious ear would be aware of it﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11, 12], and His saying: ﴿So We opened the gates of the heaven with water pouring forth﴾ ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs, and the waters met for a matter predetermined﴾ ﴿And We carried him on a [vessel] of planks and nails﴾ ﴿Sailing under Our eyes as a reward for one who had been denied﴾ ﴿And We left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 11–15].

And He explained in another place that the waves of the sea in which Allah drowned Pharaoh and his people are also like mountains, by His saying: ﴿And it parted, and each portion was like a great mountain﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 36], and at-tawd (الطَّوْد) means the great mountain.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 45:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true"﴾ — the verse.

(p-305) This noble verse indicates that this son was of the family of Noah, peace be upon him. Yet Allah, exalted is He, mentioned what indicates the opposite, when He said: ﴿O Noah, indeed he is not of your family﴾ [Hud: 46].

The answer is that the meaning of His saying, ﴿he is not of your family﴾, i.e., of those promised salvation in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will save you and your family﴾ [al-Ankabut: 33], is that he is a disbeliever, not a believer.

As for Noah's saying, ﴿indeed my son is of my family﴾, he thought him to be a Muslim among the Muslims who would be saved, as His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾ [Hud: 46]. Allah had testified that he was his son when He said: ﴿And Noah called to his son﴾ [Hud: 42]. However, He informed him that this son's deed was not righteous due to his disbelief, so he is not among the family promised salvation, although he is of the family by lineage.

The words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us﴾, and so on.

He does not specify here what the command was from which He saved Hud and those who believed with him when it came. However, He explains it in other places: it was the total annihilation by the barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim) with which Allah destroyed them, cutting off their last remnant. As in His words: (p-185) ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ ﴿It left nothing it came upon but made it like debris﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 41, 42].

And His words: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a screaming, furious wind﴾ ﴿which He imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days, in succession﴾, and so on [al-Haqqah: 6, 7].

And His words: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune﴾ ﴿uprooting people as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ [al-Qamar: 19, 20].

And His words: ﴿So We sent upon them a screaming wind during days of misfortune, that We might let them taste the punishment of disgrace﴾, and so on [Fussilat: 16].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 66:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when Our command came, We saved Salih﴾ — the verse.

And He clarified this command that came by His saying: ﴿And those who did wrong were seized by the Blast, so they were found prostrate in their homes﴾ ﴿as though they had never flourished therein. Unquestionably, [the people of] Thamud disbelieved their Lord. Unquestionably, away with Thamud!﴾ [Hud: 67, 68], and similar verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 69:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, "Peace!"﴾ — the verse.

Here he does not explain what is meant by this good tidings which the messenger angels brought to Abraham. But after this he indicated that it was the good tidings of Isaac and Jacob, in His saying: ﴿And his wife was standing, and she laughed. Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob﴾ [Hud: 71]. This is because the good tidings of righteous offspring include both the mother and the father, as His saying also indicates: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous﴾ [As-Saffat: 112].

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Do not fear; and they gave him good tidings of a knowledgeable boy"﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 28], and His saying: ﴿They said, "Do not be fearful; indeed, we give you good tidings of a knowledgeable boy"﴾. It has also been said that the good tidings is their informing him that they had been sent to destroy the people of Lot. On this view, the verses that explain it are like His saying here in this surah: ﴿They said, "Do not fear; indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lot"﴾ — the verse [Hud: 70].

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a criminal people, except the family of Lot"﴾ — the verse [Al-Hijr: 58, 59].

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a criminal people, to send upon them stones of clay"﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 32, 33], and His saying: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town; indeed, its people have been wrongdoers"﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 31].

The apparent view is the first opinion, and this last verse indicates it, because in it there is explicit statement that their informing him of the destruction of the people of Lot came after their arrival with the good tidings, since it is related to it by the conditional particle which is "lamma" (when), as you see.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then he did not delay to bring a roasted calf﴾ ﴿But when he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he considered them strange and felt a fear of them﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse, He mentions that when Abraham greeted the messenger angels, and was thinking them guests from among the sons of Adam, he hastened to them with hospitality, which was the meat of a roasted calf (ḥanīdh), meaning cooked over the fire. And when they did not eat, he felt a fear of them, so they said, "Do not fear," and informed him of their news.

In Adh-Dhariyat He explained that he turned to his family (rāgha ilā ahlihi), meaning he went to them, and brought that calf, and explained that it was fat, and that he brought it near to them, and offered them the food gently, saying to them: "Will you not eat?" [Adh-Dhariyat: 27], and that he felt a fear of them. This is in His saying: ﴿Has there come to you the story of the honored guests of Abraham? When they entered upon him and said, "Peace!" he said, "Peace, [you are] a people unknown." Then he turned to his family and brought a fat calf. And he brought it near to them and said, "Will you not eat?" But he felt a fear of them﴾ — the verse [Adh-Dhariyat: 24–28].

Note

From the story of Abraham with these guests, several matters of the etiquette of hospitality are derived. Among them is hastening the hospitality, from His saying: ﴿Then he did not delay to bring a roasted calf﴾ [Hud: 69].

Among them is that the hospitality should be from the best of what one has, because they mentioned that what he had was cattle, and the most delicious of its meat is the young, fat, tender one.

Among them is bringing the food near to the guest.

Among them is addressing him with words of utmost gentleness, like his saying "Will you not eat?" [Adh-Dhariyat: 27].

And the meaning of His saying "nakirahum" [Hud: 70] is that he disapproved of them (ankarahum) because they did not eat. The Arabs use nakira and ankara with one meaning, and the saying of al-A'sha has combined both:

"She disapproved of me, and what she disapproved of among the events was only the grey hair and the baldness."

It is related from Yunus that Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' narrated to him that he composed this line and inserted it into the poetry of al-A'sha. And Allah knows best.
